**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The AUDIT rule is directional — it constrains audits *of us*. This agreement contains no such right:

| Clause | Direction |
|---|---|
| §7.0 Audit | IBM audits MSL's Work Centers |
| §13.1 | IBM audits/inspects consigned Products |
| §21.2–21.3 | IBM inspects IBM-owned tooling |
| §24.1 | "IBM retains the right to audit" software use |
| Att. 6 §4.0 | IBM monitors/inspects MSL install locations |
| Att. 6 App. A §4 | IBM/MS audit MSL's books, 45 days' notice, independent CPA, IBM's cost unless material discrepancy, max semiannual |

MSL has no reciprocal right to audit or inspect our books, records, facilities or systems, and there is no remote-access language. §16.14 is only a mutual five-year record-retention duty — a modest recordkeeping burden, not a verification right, so it is noted rather than flagged.

I flagged one forward-looking note in the rationale: if MSL later seeks a reciprocal audit right over IBM-supplied volume or pricing data, we should hold it to the preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, MSL's cost unless >5% underpayment, no system access).
